Wow, that is such a super smart and curious question! ✨ It shows you're thinking like a real scientist! 😊

The reason scientists treat them differently is because they are actually in two different groups on nature's "family tree." You are totally right that they look very similar, but spiders (which are *arachnids*) have some key differences from insects. For example, insects always have six legs and three main body parts, while spiders have eight legs and only two main body sections. It's like comparing a turtle to a dog—they are both animals, but they have completely different body designs!

It’s a super tricky topic because nature sometimes makes things look confusingly alike! Remember, classification is just a way scientists make sure everything has a special spot in its group.
